picks.why: Soltvadkert family house whose parents and grandparents grew vines and made wine, a company in two brothers' hands since 1998 by one account and named Winery of the Year for 2015; its Kunsági Cserszegi Fűszeres is the aromatic white the house is known by.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: the house is listed at Soltvadkert by the national wine marketing body (bor.hu and winesofhungary.hu) and by the national tourism site, and a trade magazine reports its Winery of the Year award for 2015; the wine is reviewed as Frittmann Cserszegi Fűszeres 2009, Kunság, on a British critic's site, a London merchant listed the 2013 under Frittmann Testvérek, and a Hungarian grocer sells it today as Frittmann Kunsági Cserszegi Fűszeres, a dry white. The lane's 1987 was not borne out: bor.hu gives 1982 as the year of establishment and a business daily of 2011 has the brothers' company, Frittmann Testvérek, from 1998, so leave founded empty unless two sources agree on what each year was. The author confirms the house's name on the label (Frittmann or Frittmann Testvérek) and that the label carries the protected name Kunsági, which the grocer's listing shows and no label read in this run did; the Irsai Olivér, the rosé and the sparkling wines belong among the others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Kiskőrös family estate of three generations on the sand; Néró, a red grape the family took up in the early 2000s and makes as a rosé, a red and a traditional siller, is the wine the house is known by.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: the house is listed as Szentpéteri Borpince at Kiskőrös by the national wine marketing body (bor.hu and winesofhungary.hu); two accounts in English, a British drinks club's article and a Budapest business weekly, between them make Néró one of its leading grapes, made as a rosé, a red and a siller, and date the family's Néró programme to the early 2000s (the search summary did not say which account gives the date); an American wine guide's Hungarian pages list a Néró Rosé limited edition aged in wooden barrels (the 2018, in numbered bottles); and the Hungarian Parliament's wine pages name its Duna-Tisza közi Néró Rosé of 2021, from the Csábori Kétsor vineyard on a chalky base, a category winner. So the Néró found is bottled under Duna-Tisza közi, the plain's protected geographical indication and one of the names the region record covers, not under Kunsági: the author reads the label and says plainly which name it carries. The author chooses the Néró bottling the house leads with (the barrel aged rosé by the lane's account) and confirms the grape's parentage before writing it; the parentage was not searched in this run. bor.hu gives 2013 as the year of establishment beside a family history of three generations: leave founded empty unless two sources agree on what 2013 was. The region record's old vine Kadarka and Kékfrankos were not borne out; a Hungarian wine site has the house's Kadarka Blanc de Noir taking the sparkling wine prize of the Hungarian National Wine Contest of 2026, and it belongs among the others. The house writes itself Szentpéteri Borpince: confirm the label. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Soltvadkert family house with a wide range of the plain's whites, Irsai Olivér and the old Kövidinka among them, and pale rosés that have taken medals at a rosé competition in Cannes; its Kunsági Kékfrankos Rosé is the dry rosé of the sand, sold widely at home.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. IN DOUBT on the wine, as the lane said. Confirmed in the thin run: Font Pincészet is a family winery at Soltvadkert by a tourism listing and by a Hungarian grocer's pages, which sell a Font Kékfrankos Rosé and a Font Irsai Olivér today and give its grapes as Irsai Olivér, Cserszegi Fűszeres, Kövidinka, Generosa, Ezerjó and Kékfrankos; a supermarket lists a Font Kunsági Kövidinka, so the house does bottle under the protected name. The rosé with a record abroad is a different one: by a search summary that drew on the national wine marketing body's article of July 2021 on the district's rosés, Font's Kunsági Cabernet Sauvignon Rosé 2020 took gold at Le Mondial du Rosé in Cannes, and the town's own paper of September 2018 reports a silver at Cannes for the family's Cabernet Sauvignon rosé of 2017; the author reads both before using either. The Kékfrankos Rosé is kept because it is the bottling shown on sale today and the lane found it under the Kunsági name, which this run did not see on a label, nor that it is dry; if the author finds that the Cabernet Sauvignon Rosé is the wine the house leads with and still makes, tell the read together agent, who changes the pick's wine. No founding year and no history of the house was found in three searches: leave founded empty unless two sources give it, and write the story only from what is sourced. A politician of the same surname turns up in the same searches: name nobody living.

picks.why: Family estate of Szigetcsép on the Danube's Csepel island, far from the district's sandy core, its winery built in 2004 and one of the True Kunság cellars; its rosé of Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir is the wine the family is known for.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: bor.hu lists Gál Szőlőbirtok és Pincészet at Szigetcsép with 2004 as its year of establishment, and the Hungarian Parliament's wine pages give the same year for the winery, with vines at Szigetcsép, Szigetszentmárton and Szigetújfalu. The wines are entered as the district's: an international competition's results of 2024 give the Gál Rosé 2023 as Kunság, of Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir, a Swedish sommelier's notes give the Kékfrankos Rosé of 2012 and of 2014 as Kunság, and the national tourism site sets the cellar among the True Kunság family wineries and says Szigetcsép lies far from the region's core. The lane's 1994 was not borne out: a listing that reads as the house's own words says the founders built the winery after some twenty years of work for other producers, so say nothing of 1994 unless two sources give it. Two rosés turn up, the blend sold as Rosé and a Kékfrankos Rosé (the 2019 a category winner among the Parliament's wines): the author confirms which the house leads with, the label's words and the protected name on it, and gives the blend in words with no yearly shares. The author still reads the Kunság specification for Szigetcsép among its communes, which this run did not open. Not the Gál Tibor estate of Eger, nor the Gál wineries of Villány. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate between Izsák and Ágasegyháza, built up since 1999 by one account, whose head was a sparkling wine master at the Izsák sparkling works by another and which keeps to the plain's old grapes, Arany Sárfehér, Kövidinka, Ezerjó and Kadarka; its Brut is the sparkling wine it sells at home, little seen abroad.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line: the fifth pick, added in the thin run. IN DOUBT on the wine, and the merge agent rules. Confirmed, by search summaries of the national wine marketing body's article of July 2021 on the district and of the national tourism site's page on the estate, which the author reads to see which says what: the Gedeon estate near Kecskemét, its head a former sparkling wine master of the Izsák sparkling works who grows Kövidinka, Ezerjó, Sárfehér and Kadarka and makes sparkling wines and light wines with small bubbles; the tourism site also names Gedeon beside Font and Lantos among the district's houses; a business daily of 2012 sets the estate between Ágasegyháza and Izsák, growing Arany Sárfehér, Kövidinka, Ezerjó and Kadarka; and a Hungarian grocer sells a Gedeon Brut pezsgő, a Gedeon Extra Dry pezsgő and a Gedeon Irsai Olivér of 2024 today, their maker given as Gedeon Birtok Kft. of Gedeon dűlő, Izsák. Not confirmed, and the author settles each before writing: the grapes of the Brut (a wine database gives a Gedeon Birtok Cuvée, a sparkling wine filed under Kunság, as Rajnai Rizling, Arany Sárfehér and Zöldveltelini, and no source gives the Brut's), its method, and whether its label carries a protected name at all, Kunsági, Izsáki Arany Sárfehér or Duna-Tisza közi; a pezsgő may carry none. If it carries none, tell the read together agent, who moves the pick's wine to a wine of the estate that does, or rules on the pick. Little seen abroad rests only on this run finding no listing outside Hungary. No bottle sold as Izsáki Arany Sárfehér was found from this or any house in four searches, though the specification stands on the national authority's site (boraszat.kormany.hu) for still and sparkling wine of that one grape. The dates disagree: the estate built up since 1999 by one account, the company entered in November 2012 by a company register's mirror, so leave founded empty unless two agree; the accounts also disagree on the estate's size and its distance from Kecskemét, which no record needs. Standbys, none with a wine confirmed: Royalsekt, the Izsák sparkling works itself (founded in the 1950s and a sparkling plant since the 1970s by its trade fair profile on the wine body's site, its Arany Sárfehér pezsgő named in a consumer test of 2018 and not found on sale since), Lantos at Soltvadkert (2009 by bor.hu), and Polyák and Kunvin, both of which turned up on winesofhungary.hu in a search of the district's houses and were not looked into. Name no living member of the family.
